source: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/0000-XXXX-Robot-Template (76 Java files, ~9.6k LOC incl. 1946-line vendored LimelightHelpers; git history: 3 commits, "Initial commit" + a Fable-5 code-review fix pass)
summary: This is a dense, opinionated, genuinely good template — not vendor boilerplate. It is deliberately STATE-BASED, not command-based: subsystems are plain actuator classes (no SubsystemBase, no Commands, no Triggers), a single `Superstructure` state machine drives every mechanism from a 12-value `SuperState` enum, and `RobotContainer` polls `XboxController` directly. WPILib's CommandScheduler runs only for the two external tools that require it (PathPlanner autos/pathfinding and SysId). Every mechanism AND the swerve drivetrain sit behind a hand-rolled AdvantageKit IO trio (`XxxIO` interface with an `@AutoLog XxxIOInputs` inner class + default no-op methods, `XxxIOTalonFX` that also hosts the physics sim, `XxxIONeo`, and an anonymous `new XxxIO(){}` for REPLAY), so the whole robot replays deterministically; 10 mechanisms + swerve = ~14 `Logger.processInputs` sites and ~10 near-identical TalonFX config blocks. Everything — CAN IDs, gear ratios, gains, presets, soft limits, sim masses, vision config, logging indices — lives in ONE 712-line `Constants.java` of nested `static final class` sections annotated with a hand-rolled `ADD` / `VERIFY` / `TUNE` marker convention and a unit in every trailing comment. The single biggest cost is per-mechanism copy-paste: the same `TalonFXConfiguration` + cached-StatusSignal + `optimizeBusUtilization` + sim-advance block, the same `private enum ControlMode {POSITION, DUTY_CYCLE, NEUTRAL}` (5 verbatim copies), the same clamp/`setManual`/`holdCurrentX`/`isAtTarget` bodies, the same `/ 360.0` degree↔rotation conversion inlined 41 times, and a 9-line nested-ternary IO selector in RobotContainer. Tuning is 100% redeploy-based — every gain is a compile-time `static final`, no IO exposes a `setGains`, and the author's own `LoggedTunableNumber`/`LoggedTunableBoolean` are never called anywhere in the repo (alongside `GeomUtil`, `EqualsUtil`, `AutoAlign`, and a `RobotState` singleton that is written but never read).
stack: WPILib/GradleRIO 2026.2.1, Java 17 (`sourceCompatibility = VERSION_17`), Gradle pinned to `C:/Users/Public/wpilib/2026/jdk` via gradle.properties. Vendordeps: AdvantageKit 26.0.2 (+ `akit-autolog` annotationProcessor whose version is parsed out of `vendordeps/AdvantageKit.json` at build time by a JsonSlurper in build.gradle so it can't drift), CTRE Phoenix 6 v26.3.0, REVLib 2026.0.5, PathplannerLib 2026.1.2, photonlib v2026.2.2, WPILib-New-Commands 1.0.0. LimelightHelpers is vendored as source (`frc/robot/LimelightHelpers.java`, 1946 lines). Elastic.java is vendored from Gold872 (2-space indent, unlike the rest of the repo). Hardware model: Kraken X60/TalonFX everywhere by default, Pigeon 2, CANcoder (FusedCANcoder for steer), CTRE CANdle for LEDs, SDS MK4i L3+ swerve (DRIVE_GEAR_RATIO 5.357142857142857, TURN 150.0/7.0), Spark MAX/NEO as a full parallel IO set. Tests: JUnit 5.10.1, `forkEvery = 1` (sim CAN rejects duplicate device IDs in one JVM). Deploy assets: PathPlanner autos incl. a 7-auto "Swerve Tests" diagnostic suite, a Choreo `Demo.traj`, `elastic-layout.json` served over `WebServer.start(5800, ...)`.

patterns.name: AdvantageKit IO trio (interface + @AutoLog inputs + no-op default methods)
patterns.whatItDoes: Every mechanism package is `XxxIO.java` (interface holding an `@AutoLog class XxxIOInputs` POJO of everything read FROM hardware, plus `default void` no-op output methods), `XxxIOTalonFX.java` (real hardware AND physics sim in one class), `XxxIONeo.java`, and `Xxx.java` (the subsystem, which calls `io.updateInputs(inputs); Logger.processInputs("Arm", inputs);` then makes every decision from `inputs`, never from hardware). REPLAY passes an anonymous `new ArmIO(){}` so all inputs come from the log.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/0000-XXXX-Robot-Template/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/arm/ArmIO.java (canonical, most-documented copy — other IOs literally say "See {@code arm.ArmIO} for the pattern"); repeated for elevator, wrist, turret, shooter, intake, indexer, endeffector, climber, vision, swerve/ModuleIO, swerve/GyroIO
patterns.libraryValue: This is the single most-repeated structure in the repo (11 copies). PumpkinLib should ship the inputs struct + the subsystem shell as generics/base classes (`PositionMechanism`, `VelocityMechanism`, `RollerMechanism`) so a team writes only the hardware-specific config, not the 40-line ceremony. The `default {}` no-op convention for the REPLAY IO is the exact right primitive to keep.

patterns.name: Three-mode IO selection driven by one `Mode` enum
patterns.whatItDoes: `Constants.LoggingConstants.getMode()` returns `RobotBase.isReal() ? REAL : SIM_MODE` where `SIM_MODE` is a hand-edited constant (SIM or REPLAY). RobotContainer then builds each subsystem's IO from that mode crossed with a per-mechanism `MOTOR_TYPE` constant.
patterns.whereSeen: Constants.java lines 683-711 (LoggingConstants, Mode enum, getMode()); RobotContainer.java lines 137-218; Robot.java lines 42-64 (logger receivers per mode)
patterns.libraryValue: The intent ("one constant swaps motor family; one enum swaps REAL/SIM/REPLAY") is excellent; the expression of it is nine copies of a nested ternary that is trivially easy to typo. A library should own this as `IOFactory.select(mode, motorType, krakenSupplier, neoSupplier, simSupplier)` or an annotation/registry, and it should also fix the current wart that SIM silently ignores MOTOR_TYPE (the NEO IOs have no sim at all).

patterns.name: Single-file Constants with unit comments, ADD/VERIFY/TUNE markers, and a CAN ID map header
patterns.whatItDoes: One 712-line `Constants.java`, nested `public static final class XxxConstants` per subsystem, private ctor on the outer class. Every value carries its unit in a trailing comment and a marker: TUNE (a gain to dial in), VERIFY (a physical measurement), ADD (something you must supply). The file header contains a hand-maintained ASCII CAN ID map (1=Pigeon, 2/3/4=FL drive/steer/cancoder, ... 26=EndEffector) and a conventions block explaining that Phoenix 6 gains are voltage-based with error in mechanism rotations.
patterns.libraryValue: The ADD/VERIFY/TUNE taxonomy is a real, reusable idea — a library could formalize it as annotations or a config record with required/measured/tunable fields, and generate a first-setup checklist or a startup Alert for anything still at its placeholder. The derived-constant style (`INCHES_PER_DRUM_ROTATION = circumference * stages`) is exactly the shape a `LinearMechanismGeometry` value type should take.

patterns.name: Preset enums carrying a unit-typed payload
patterns.whatItDoes: Setpoints are not loose doubles; each mechanism declares a nested `enum Preset` whose constants hold a value and expose it through a unit-named accessor, and the subsystem takes the enum directly.
patterns.whereSeen: Constants.java ElevatorConstants.Preset (lines 282-287), ArmConstants.Preset (334-339), WristConstants.Preset (380-385); consumed in Elevator.setGoal / Arm.setGoal / Wrist.setGoal and Superstructure.stowElevatorArmWrist()
patterns.libraryValue: Cheap, type-safe, and self-documenting at the call site (`elevator.setGoal(Preset.HIGH)`). A library should generalize it to a `Setpoint<Distance>` / `Setpoint<Angle>` (or WPILib Units `Measure`) so presets, soft limits, and tolerances all share one unit-checked type instead of bare doubles.

patterns.name: Superstructure state machine with an on-entry latch
patterns.whatItDoes: A 12-state enum (`IDLE, INTAKE, HOLD, EJECT, AIM, SHOOT, SCORE_LOW/MID/HIGH, CLIMB_DEPLOY, CLIMB, MANUAL`); `periodic()` computes `boolean onEntry = state != prevState` then calls `applyState(state, onEntry)`, a giant switch that pushes setpoints to every mechanism every loop. `resetStateEntry()` re-arms the latch on disable so IDLE's entry action (capturing the climber hold position) fires again.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/0000-XXXX-Robot-Template/src/main/java/frc/robot/Superstructure.java lines 130-246; resetStateEntry called from RobotContainer.setDisabled() line 448
patterns.libraryValue: The onEntry latch + the disable-time re-arm is a subtle, hard-won detail worth owning in a library (`StateMachine<S>` with onEnter/whileIn/onExit hooks). It would also kill the current footgun where every case must remember to zero every actuator (see pain points).

patterns.name: Hand-rolled AdvantageKit-native swerve (GyroIO + 4 ModuleIO + PhoenixOdometryThread)
patterns.whatItDoes: Deliberately replaces CTRE's SwerveDrivetrain wrapper so the drivetrain replays. `Swerve` owns a `GyroIO` + four `Module`s, WPILib `SwerveDriveKinematics` + `SwerveDrivePoseEstimator`, feeds EVERY high-frequency odometry sample into the estimator, falls back to twist-integrated heading when the gyro is absent, caches measured states/speeds once per loop, and exposes SysId. `PhoenixOdometryThread` is a singleton daemon thread that `waitForAll`s on CAN FD or polls at ODOMETRY_FREQUENCY_HZ on the rio bus, with a `ReentrantLock odometryLock` that Swerve holds while draining.
patterns.whereSeen: subsystems/swerve/Swerve.java (293 lines), Module.java, ModuleIO.java, ModuleIOTalonFX.java, ModuleIONeo.java, ModuleIOSim.java, PhoenixOdometryThread.java (141 lines), GyroIOPigeon2.java
patterns.libraryValue: This is 800+ lines of infrastructure every team re-copies from 6328 and gets subtly wrong (sample-count alignment, the CAN-FD-vs-rio branch, the odometry lock, cosine-scaled setpoints, the non-mutating optimize copy). It is the highest-value single thing PumpkinLib could absorb wholesale — ideally parameterized only by a `SwerveConfig` record + a `ModuleConfig[]`.

patterns.name: Single-source swerve gains in physical units, converted per-controller inside each IO
patterns.whatItDoes: DRIVE_kS/kV/kA/kP and TURN_kP/kD are declared once in VOLTS per WHEEL RADIAN(/s). ModuleIOTalonFX multiplies by 2π (its loop runs in wheel rotations via SensorToMechanismRatio); ModuleIONeo divides by 12 (voltage-compensated duty-cycle loop). A unit test pins the invariant.
patterns.whereSeen: Constants.java lines 179-194 (declaration + a CAUTION about Tuner X emitting rotor-referenced gains); ModuleIOTalonFX.java lines 79-98; ModuleIONeo.java lines 62-84; src/test/java/frc/robot/SwerveUnitTest.java
patterns.libraryValue: A gain-unit type (`Gains.perWheelRadian(...)` that knows how to emit Phoenix-rotation and REV-duty-cycle forms) would make this trap structurally impossible instead of a comment plus a test. Note the honest caveat the author already wrote: kD's derivative time base differs between controllers and does NOT convert exactly.

patterns.name: Shoot-on-the-move solver (AimingCalculator) with record result + interpolating lookup tables
patterns.whatItDoes: Game-agnostic ballistic solver: takes pose, field ChassisSpeeds, field acceleration, and a Translation3d target; computes the off-center launch point's velocity (including the tangential term chassis omega adds), projects release velocity over a 0.05 s latency, then iterates 5 times over a virtual target leading by v_release × flight_time. Distance→flywheelRps / launchAngle / flightTime come from `double[][]` tables loaded into `InterpolatingDoubleTreeMap`.
patterns.whereSeen: util/AimingCalculator.java (139 lines); tables in Constants.ShooterConstants.DISTANCE_TO_FLYWHEEL_RPS / _LAUNCH_ANGLE_DEG / _FLIGHT_TIME_SEC; driven from Superstructure.aim(); pinned by src/test/java/frc/robot/AimingCalculatorTest.java
patterns.libraryValue: Genuinely reusable and already game-agnostic. The `double[][]` → InterpolatingDoubleTreeMap idiom is worth a first-class `LookupTable` type in the library (with a `fromCsv`/`fromTestShots` builder), and the record-returning solver is the right API shape.

patterns.name: Centralized Dashboard + the `Draggables/` @AutoLogOutput folder
patterns.whatItDoes: Exactly one class publishes NetworkTables/Elastic/Glass data; subsystems expose plain getters and know nothing about the dashboard. It also gathers every field-space pose worth dropping into AdvantageScope 3D into one autologged `Draggables/` table (RobotPose, RobotPose3d, Components, ZeroedComponents, AimTarget, AutoPreview, ActivePath, TargetPose), plus a Mechanism2d, cached swerve-widget NT entries, PathPlannerLogging callbacks that clear while disabled, and WPILib `Alert`s.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/0000-XXXX-Robot-Template/src/main/java/frc/robot/Dashboard.java (311 lines); LoggingConstants component indices in Constants.java lines 683-691; asserted end-to-end by src/test/java/frc/robot/AutoLogOutputTest.java
patterns.libraryValue: The `Draggables/` convention and the articulated-component Pose3d[] publishing are pure boilerplate every team rewrites. A library `ComponentPublisher` (register a ligament with its parent transform and a supplier) plus a standard Draggables table would remove ~150 lines per robot and the hand-maintained index constants (`ELEVATOR_CARRIAGE_INDEX = 0`).

patterns.name: Auto chooser of NAMES (not Commands) + Choreo discovery + disabled path preview + vision-aware start-pose seeding
patterns.whatItDoes: `LoggedDashboardChooser<String>` stores auto NAMES so the choice is AKit-logged/replayed and the Command is rebuilt fresh on every enable (WPILib forbids reusing a composed Command). Choreo `.traj` files in deploy/choreo are auto-discovered, validated by parsing, and offered as `"Choreo: <name>"`. The selected auto's poses are reloaded on selection/alliance change and drawn on the Elastic field while disabled. Start pose is seeded ONLY when `vision.hasRecentFix()` is false — every `.auto` ships with `"resetOdom": false`.
patterns.whereSeen: RobotContainer.java lines 134, 196-200, 322-443; Vision.hasRecentFix() in subsystems/vision/Vision.java lines 97-106; pinned by src/test/java/frc/robot/AutoPreviewTest.java and RobotContainerTest
patterns.libraryValue: Three separate well-known bugs are solved here in one place (Command reuse, replay-unsafe chooser reads, autos snapping odometry away from a good vision fix). A library `AutoManager` should own all of it, including the preview-poses cache and the graceful `List.of()` degradation on an unparseable name.

patterns.name: Small hardened utilities: PhoenixUtil.tryUntilOk, AllianceFlipUtil, LocalADStarAK
patterns.whatItDoes: `tryUntilOk(5, () -> motor.getConfigurator().apply(config))` retries a config apply on a busy boot-time CAN bus (used in all 10 TalonFX IOs — but notably NOT in ModuleIOTalonFX/ModuleIONeo/GyroIOPigeon2, which call `apply` bare). `AllianceFlipUtil` delegates to PathPlanner's `FlippingUtil` so robot code flips exactly the way the paths do, with an added Translation3d overload that preserves Z. `LocalADStarAK` wraps PathPlanner's pathfinder in a `LoggableInputs` so on-the-fly pathfinding replays.
patterns.whereSeen: util/PhoenixUtil.java, util/AllianceFlipUtil.java, util/LocalADStarAK.java (118 lines, credited to Team 6328); registered in Robot.java line 69
patterns.libraryValue: All three are library-grade already. tryUntilOk should be the ONLY way the library applies a config (so it can't be forgotten, as it was in the swerve IOs), and should raise a WPILib `Alert` rather than printing to stderr where nobody sees it.

patterns.name: Test suite that pins architectural invariants, not just math
patterns.whatItDoes: Seven JUnit 5 classes with narrative Javadoc explaining which regression each one pins: whole-robot construct + 5 loops + repeat-enable command freshness; Choreo parse; elevator IO-sim bounded through open/closed loop; end-to-end assertion that every `@AutoLogOutput` key actually reaches the log (driven through `Logger.AdvancedHooks` with `disableRobotBaseCheck()`); auto/Choreo option resolution incl. null/unknown degrading to empty; shoot-on-move physics; swerve gain units + non-mutating `runSetpoint`.

painPoints.problem: Ten near-identical TalonFX IO classes, each hand-writing the same config + StatusSignal + bus-optimization + sim-advance ceremony
painPoints.evidence: `InvertedValue.Clockwise_Positive : InvertedValue.CounterClockwise_Positive` appears in 10 files (12 occurrences); `SupplyCurrentLimitEnable = true` 10x; `optimizeBusUtilization()` 16x; `BaseStatusSignal.setUpdateFrequencyForAll(50.0, ...)` + `temperature.setUpdateFrequency(4.0)` repeated verbatim in ArmIOTalonFX:83-87, WristIOTalonFX:73-75, TurretIOTalonFX:69-71, ClimberIOTalonFX:67-69, ElevatorIOTalonFX:95-101, IntakeIOTalonFX:56-60, ShooterIOTalonFX:53-57, IndexerIOTalonFX:41-42, EndEffectorIOTalonFX:42-43. The sim block is also copy-pasted: `var simState = motor.getSimState(); simState.setSupplyVoltage(RobotController.getBatteryVoltage()); sim.setInputVoltage(simState.getMotorVoltage()); sim.update(0.02); simState.setRawRotorPosition(Units.radiansToRotations(...) * GEAR_RATIO); simState.setRotorVelocity(...)` in Arm/Wrist/Turret/Climber/Intake IOTalonFX.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `TalonFXMechanism` builder that takes (id, bus, inverted, neutralMode, currentLimits, sensorToMechanismRatio, Slot0 gains, gravity type, MotionMagic profile, soft limits) and returns a pre-wired device with cached signals at the right rates, plus a `SimAdapter` that advances any `LinearSystemSim`/`SingleJointedArmSim`/`ElevatorSim`/`FlywheelSim`/`DCMotorSim` against the device's sim state. Each mechanism IO should shrink to ~15 lines.

painPoints.problem: `private enum ControlMode { POSITION, DUTY_CYCLE, NEUTRAL }` plus the identical clamp/setManual/holdCurrent/isAtTarget bodies are duplicated verbatim across 5 subsystems
painPoints.evidence: Identical enum declared in Arm.java:23, Elevator.java:15, Wrist.java:16, Turret.java:16, Climber.java:15. The `setManual` body is byte-for-byte the same modulo constant names in Arm.java:61-68, Wrist.java:49-56, Turret.java:57-64, Climber.java:50-57, Elevator.java:48-55. The `isAtTarget()` body `Math.abs(inputs.positionX - targetX) <= XConstants.ALLOWED_ERROR` appears 6 times.
painPoints.libraryFix: One `PositionMechanism` base (or a composed `SetpointController`) owning mode, clamped target, manual-with-hold-on-release, at-target tolerance, and the `@AutoLogOutput` target/atTarget getters — parameterized by a units/geometry object. Removes ~250 lines and the risk of the copies drifting.

painPoints.problem: Degree↔rotation and inch↔rotation conversions are inlined by hand everywhere instead of living in one converter
painPoints.evidence: `360.0` appears 41 times across src/main. E.g. ArmIOTalonFX.java:69-73 `config.MotionMagic.MotionMagicCruiseVelocity = ArmConstants.MAX_VELOCITY / 360.0;` ... `SoftwareLimitSwitch.ForwardSoftLimitThreshold = ArmConstants.MAX_ANGLE / 360.0;` and :114 `inputs.positionDeg = position.getValueAsDouble() * 360.0;` — repeated identically in WristIOTalonFX, TurretIOTalonFX, IntakeIOTalonFX. Elevator has its own private pair (`inchesToRotations`/`rotationsToInches`, ElevatorIOTalonFX:113-114) that nothing else can reuse.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `MechanismUnits`/`Ratio` value type (or lean on WPILib `Measure<Angle>`/`Measure<Distance>`) that the library uses for every setpoint, soft limit, MotionMagic profile value, and input read. One misplaced `/360.0` today is a silent 360x error.

painPoints.problem: Adding or removing one mechanism requires edits in at least seven places
painPoints.evidence: README.md lines 438-447 documents it as the workflow: "copy the closest subsystems/<name> package ..., construct it in RobotContainer with the REAL/SIM/REPLAY IO selector, drive it from a SuperState, and add its telemetry to Dashboard." Concretely that is: a Constants section; the 4-file package; a `RobotContainer` field (line 118-126) + the ternary in the ctor (154-171) + a line in `periodic()` (226-234) + a line in `setDisabled()` (450-459); a `Dashboard` constructor arg (14 positional params, Dashboard.java:121-123) + field + `publishMechanismTelemetry()` lines; `Superstructure` ctor (10 params, line 91-92) + every relevant `case`; and the hardcoded expected-key list in AutoLogOutputTest.java:79-106.
painPoints.libraryFix: A subsystem registry: mechanisms self-register (name, IO, periodic, stop, telemetry suppliers) so `periodic()`/`setDisabled()`/dashboard publishing/log-key assertions are derived, not hand-maintained. Also kills the 14-arg Dashboard and 10-arg Superstructure constructors.

painPoints.problem: Live tuning is impossible — every gain is a compile-time constant, and the author's own tunable classes are dead code
painPoints.evidence: `grep -rn LoggedTunableNumber|LoggedTunableBoolean src/` returns only their own definitions and Javadoc — zero call sites. No IO exposes a `setGains`/`applyGains`; gains are read once in each IO constructor (e.g. ArmIOTalonFX.java:62-67 `config.Slot0.kP = ArmConstants.kP;`). `LoggedTunableNumber`'s own Javadoc says "Use it while dialing in a gain, then paste the final value into Constants" but no mechanism wires it. Same for `GeomUtil`, `EqualsUtil`, `AutoAlign` (never called), and `RobotState` (written by Swerve.java:190, never read).
painPoints.libraryFix: Make tunability the default path: every library mechanism publishes its gains as tunables under `/Tuning/<Subsystem>/kP` in a dev/tuning build, polls `hasChanged()` in periodic, and re-applies via a mandatory `IO.setGains(...)`. Ship a one-flag switch between 'tunable' and 'frozen constants' so the same code compiles for competition.

painPoints.problem: Robot geometry is duplicated between Constants.java and PathPlanner's settings.json and must be kept in sync by hand
painPoints.evidence: Constants.java: `TRACK_WIDTH_METERS = Units.inchesToMeters(24.75)` = 0.62865, `WHEEL_RADIUS_METERS = inchesToMeters(2.0)` = 0.0508, `DRIVE_GEAR_RATIO = 5.357142857142857`, `MAX_LINEAR_SPEED_MPS = 5.96`, `DRIVE_STATOR_CURRENT_LIMIT = 90.0`. deploy/pathplanner/settings.json: `robotTrackwidth: 0.628`, `driveWheelRadius: 0.051`, `driveGearing: 5.36`, `maxDriveSpeed: 5.96`, `driveCurrentLimit: 90.0`, plus module X/Y of ±0.314. Constants.java line 168 says outright "keep settings.json 'maxDriveSpeed' in sync"; README line 337 repeats it. `Swerve.configureAutoBuilder()` then loads `RobotConfig.fromGUISettings()` — so the JSON, not Constants, is what PathPlanner actually believes.
painPoints.libraryFix: Either generate settings.json from the Java config at build/deploy time, or have the library read the JSON as the single source and derive Constants from it — plus a startup consistency check that raises an Alert when the two disagree beyond a tolerance.

painPoints.problem: Every Superstructure state must remember to reset every actuator; forgetting one leaves hardware running
painPoints.evidence: Superstructure.java case MANUAL:220-222 has the comment "Don't leave rollers running at whatever the previous state set." case EJECT:176 has "entering from AIM/SHOOT must spin the flywheels down". The IDLE, INTAKE, HOLD cases each repeat the same four lines (`intake.retract(); intake.setRollerSpeed(0); indexer.stop(); endEffector.stop();`). AIM (183-187) notably does NOT call `intake.retract()` or touch the endEffector — an asymmetry that is invisible until it bites.
painPoints.libraryFix: Invert the model: each loop the library writes DEFAULT outputs for every mechanism, then the active state overrides only what it cares about. That makes 'forgot to stop the roller' structurally impossible and shrinks each case to its actual intent.

painPoints.problem: The NEO path is real code that is never simulated or tested
painPoints.evidence: RobotContainer.java:151-152 comments "SIM: ALWAYS the TalonFX IO - it hosts the physics sim (the NEO IOs have none)"; the ternaries gate on `!sim &&`. No `XxxIONeo` constructs any WPILib sim. Every NEO IO hardcodes `inputs.connected = true` (ArmIONeo:60, ElevatorIONeo:72-73, ShooterIONeo:60-61, TurretIONeo:53, ClimberIONeo:52, IntakeIONeo:67/73, ModuleIONeo:100/106 — "Spark MAX has no cheap connection signal"). TurretIONeo.setAngle:62-64 silently drops the chassis-omega feedforward. ModuleIONeo:114-117 emits one odometry sample per loop from `Timer.getFPGATimestamp()` (not the AKit-deterministic `Timer.getTimestamp()` used elsewhere).
painPoints.libraryFix: Give the library's REV backend the same sim support and a real connection/fault check (Spark `getFaults`/`getStickyFaults` or a warning-counter heartbeat), and unify the timestamp source. Otherwise the 'switch one constant to NEO' promise ships untested code to a competition.

painPoints.problem: Wrist manual control hardcodes magic numbers because WristConstants lacks the fields every sibling has
painPoints.evidence: Wrist.java:50-51 — `if (Math.abs(stickInput) >= 0.1) { manualOutput = stickInput * 0.15; }`. Every other mechanism uses named constants (`ArmConstants.MANUAL_DEADBAND`, `MANUAL_SPEED_LIMIT`, etc.), but Constants.WristConstants (lines 356-390) defines no MANUAL_* fields at all. Also, `Wrist.setManual`, `Turret.setManual`, `Climber.setManual`, `Elevator.resetEncoder()`, and `Climber.retractFully()` are never called from anywhere — Superstructure MANUAL only drives elevator + arm.
painPoints.libraryFix: A shared mechanism config record with required manual-control fields makes the omission a compile error rather than a silently different feel on one joint. Dead setters disappear once manual control is a library feature toggled per mechanism.

painPoints.problem: Boot position seeding trusts that mechanisms are parked at a known hard stop, with no absolute encoder anywhere
painPoints.evidence: ArmIOTalonFX.java:76 `motor.setPosition(ArmConstants.START_ANGLE / 360.0);`, WristIOTalonFX:66, IntakeIOTalonFX:48, TurretIOTalonFX:62 `motor.setPosition(0)`, ClimberIOTalonFX:60, ElevatorIOTalonFX:83-84. Constants.java:324 states the assumption: "The arm is seeded to START_ANGLE at boot (assumes it rests on a known hard stop)." Sensors.java sections 6 and 7 document how to add a Through Bore / CANcoder to fix this, but nothing is wired — and the fused-CANcoder pattern is only used in ModuleIOTalonFX.
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship first-class homing strategies (absolute-encoder seed, current-limit homing, limit-switch homing) as a pluggable `ZeroingStrategy` on every position mechanism, with the fused-CANcoder config already correct.

painPoints.problem: Alerts/errors go to places nobody watches, and only two alerts exist for a 10-mechanism robot
painPoints.evidence: PhoenixUtil.java:27 prints a config failure to `System.err`. Swerve.java:124 and RobotContainer.java:367/397 use `DriverStation.reportError`. Dashboard.java:116-119 defines exactly two WPILib `Alert`s (low battery, elevator sides out of sync) — despite every IO already logging a `connected` boolean and a `temperatureCelsius` that nothing consumes.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `HealthMonitor` that auto-registers an Alert per device from the IO inputs the library already collects (disconnected, over-temp, config-apply failure, follower disagreement, CAN utilization) — zero per-robot wiring.

painPoints.problem: A few smaller correctness/consistency traps worth designing out
painPoints.evidence: (a) `SwerveConstants.MAX_ANGULAR_SPEED_RAD_PER_SEC` is derived from track width but the driver also multiplies by `ROTATION_SPEED_SCALE` in RobotContainer:255 while translation uses `DRIVE_SPEED_SCALE` — two unrelated scalars with no shared clamp. (b) Constants.ArmConstants.SIM_SIMULATE_GRAVITY = false and kG = 0.0 with the comment that Arm_Cosine "is only correct when 0 deg = arm horizontal" — a real convention landmine left to the user. (c) `Swerve.addVisionMeasurement` reaches for a fully-qualified `frc.robot.Constants.VisionConstants.MAX_ANGULAR_SPEED_FOR_VISION` (line 282) instead of importing, a hint the vision gate lives in the wrong layer. (d) ModuleIOTalonFX/ModuleIONeo/GyroIOPigeon2 apply configs WITHOUT `PhoenixUtil.tryUntilOk`, unlike all 10 mechanism IOs. (e) `Vision.stdDevs` uses a literal `9999999` sentinel for 'don't trust heading' (Vision.java:87) and a magic `1.0 + d*d/30.0` distance scale (line 82).
painPoints.libraryFix: Own the angle-convention contract (declare where zero is and whether gravity is cosine- or static-type, and derive the Phoenix GravityType from it), make retrying config application the only code path, and express vision trust as a named, tunable `TrustModel` instead of sentinels and inline polynomials.

constraints: WPILib 2026 / GradleRIO 2026.2.1 and Java 17 exactly (build.gradle sets sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility VERSION_17; gradle.properties pins org.gradle.java.home to the WPILib JDK because a foreign JAVA_HOME hard-crashes test JVMs loading wpiHal). PumpkinLib must compile on Java 17 — no Java 21 features.

AdvantageKit deterministic replay is non-negotiable and shapes every API: anything read from hardware MUST pass through an @AutoLog inputs struct, subsystems must decide only from `inputs`, and time must come from `Timer.getTimestamp()` not `Timer.getFPGATimestamp()` (explicitly called out in Superstructure.java:85-87 and Vision.java:73-75). Any library abstraction that hides a direct hardware read breaks replay and will be rejected.

AdvantageKit's `@AutoLog` annotation processor generates `XxxIOInputsAutoLogged` from a class in the user's source tree; the akit-autolog version is pulled out of vendordeps/AdvantageKit.json at build time. A library shipping pre-generated or generic input structs must not fight this processor, and AutoLogOutputManager only discovers `@AutoLogOutput` fields reachable from the robot object graph AND inside the `frc.robot` package — a `pumpkinlib.*` package will NOT be auto-scanned unless the library handles registration itself.

State-based, not command-based. No mechanism may be a Command/SubsystemBase/Trigger. `Swerve implements Subsystem` only so SysId and PathPlanner can `require` it; the CommandScheduler is allowed to run ONLY PathPlanner autos/pathfinding, SysId, and PathPlanner warmup. A command-factory-first library API would be rejected outright.

Every mechanism and the swerve modules must support BOTH Kraken X60/TalonFX (Phoenix 6 v26.3.0) and NEO/Spark MAX (REVLib 2026.0.5), switchable by exactly one constant, sharing one set of CAN IDs, offsets, and physically-expressed gains.

Vision must remain backend-swappable between Limelight (vendored LimelightHelpers, MegaTag1 while disabled / MegaTag2 while enabled) and PhotonVision (photonlib v2026.2.2) behind a single constant, producing identical logged observation arrays.

Autonomous is PathPlannerLib 2026.1.2 + Choreo `.traj` through the same chooser, with `Pathfinding.setPathfinder(new LocalADStarAK())` and `RobotConfig.fromGUISettings()` — so deploy/pathplanner/settings.json remains an external source of truth the library must reconcile with, not replace.

The project must build, `./gradlew test`, and `simulateJava` out of the box with placeholder values and team number 0 — a library that requires real CAN IDs or measured constants before it compiles breaks the template's core promise.

Unit tests fork one JVM per class (`forkEvery = 1`) because simulated CAN devices reject duplicate IDs in a process, and AdvantageKit's Logger cannot restart within a JVM (AutoLogOutputTest must stay single-@Test). Any library test helpers must respect both limits.

The one-file `Constants.java` is a deliberate, documented design decision ("THE ONE AND ONLY CONSTANTS FILE"), as is the ADD/VERIFY/TUNE marker convention and a unit in every trailing comment. A library that scatters configuration across many files, or replaces it with YAML/JSON, works against the author's stated intent.

Style to match: 4-space indent, ALL_CAPS_SNAKE constants EXCEPT gains which are literally `kP, kI, kD, kS, kV, kG`; units baked into identifiers (`_METERS`, `_INCHES`, `Deg`, `RadPerSec`, `Rps`, `Amps`, `Celsius`); human units (inches/degrees) at the API boundary with rotations confined inside the IO; `record`s for value types (ModuleConfig, ShotParameters); enums-with-payload for presets; one-line method bodies for trivial overrides (`@Override public void setNeutral() { motor.setControl(neutralRequest); }`); a teaching-grade Javadoc block on EVERY class explaining WHY; no `m_` prefixes outside the WPILib-generated Robot.java; ASCII only, no emoji.

No CLAUDE.md exists in this repo; .claude/settings.local.json contains only a single Bash permission entry. There is no project-specific agent guidance to conform to beyond the README (487 lines) and the in-code Javadoc.
